description: Coverage of the required cardinality variants for every inventoried collection field. Derived from the run that produced it, not asserted by hand.

coverageDimensions.boundaryNormalizer: The field is driven through the shared stage contract at this cardinality and judged by the validator named in boundaryValidator: collectionShape rows go through the list normalizer, shape validator, and a JSON round trip; mapShape rows go through the map shape validator and a JSON round trip and are never normalized, because there is no correct rewrite from an array or a scalar to a keyed object.
coverageDimensions.producerPath: The row is driven at this cardinality through the registered stage contract its shipping producer calls, via the production builder in src/Agents/reviewer/StageProducers.ps1, and - for every stage whose producer runs without a live capture or a model - through the shipping producer function itself. The status is read back out of the shared contract ledger, which records the element count the boundary actually judged, so a cell states what was published rather than that a validator returned.

producerPathLegend.producerCensusMatched: The shipping producer ran and the boundary judged a census whose element count equals the cardinality the harness constructed.
producerPathLegend.producerCensusReshaped: The shipping producer ran and the boundary judged its census, but the count differs from the constructed input because the producer legitimately reshapes it - deduplicating, unioning, or folding duplicates. producerObservedCensus records what the boundary actually saw.
producerPathLegend.boundaryRefusal: Not a census at all: the null-vs-missing and wrong-scalar variants are shapes a producer must never publish, and the evidence is the stage boundary refusing them by name before any consumer runs. These cells are never counted as producer-invoked cardinalities.
producerPathLegend.boundaryOnly: The registered boundary ran through the production builder, but the producing function needs a live capture and was not executed.
producerPathLegend.failed: The drive raised, which fails the suite.

producerEquivalenceLegend.direct: The function this row names as its producer is the function wired to the stage boundary, so the row is covered by its own call site.
producerEquivalenceLegend.stageBoundaryEquivalent: The row is covered through the same registered boundary its stage publishes through, driven by the production builder, but not through this row's own call site.
producerEquivalenceLegend.unbound: No shipping boundary publishes this row's stage. This value must never appear.

fullCoverageRule: fullCoverageClaimed may only be true when every inventoried field reports covered for every variant in the boundary dimension, every producer cell reports producerCensusMatched, no row is covered only through a stage-boundary equivalent, no boundary carries a residual, and every producer is reachable from shipping code.

escapeShapes.description: A function returning a locally built empty set bare hands back $null, so an empty result is indistinguishable from a failed one.
A one-element set returned bare arrives as a bare scalar, so a later .Count reads the string length instead of the element count.
Wrapping a protected collection return in @() nests it as one element, so an index built from it collapses to a single bogus entry.
The same wrap turns an empty protected return into a one-element array, so an empty result is counted as one.
A JSON document whose root is an array is emitted as bare objects, so a one-element document reads as a single object and an empty one as nothing at all.
An empty evidenceFactIds array must survive the boundary as [] rather than as null, so an unsupported candidate stays distinguishable from an unread one.
A Where-Object difference that matches nothing yields $null, so a later Sort or .Count on the exact-key difference fails under StrictMode.
A difference set with one survivor arrives as a bare scalar, so the count of remaining exact-key differences reads as a string length.
Empty and one-element configuration arrays keep their cardinality across a write and a read, so an absent option never reads as a present one.
An empty ExistingFingerprints set must reach the caller as an empty set, because $null would be read as "no prior state observed" instead of "no prior findings".
A source reader returning zero, one, or many entries keeps its cardinality when the caller assigns the protected return instead of wrapping it.

sabotage.incidentClass: A set built locally and returned bare, so an empty result reached the caller as $null.
A protected collection return wrapped in @(), which nested it as one element and collapsed an index.
A closure calling a repository function by name, which GetNewClosure does not capture.
A contract serialized without an explicit depth, so nested structures were truncated to type names.
A contract written to a file without an explicit compact decision, leaving its on-disk form implicit.
A cardinality read taken straight off a pipeline, so a single match counted as its own length.
A non-preserved command result assigned and counted later, so an empty result became $null.
A script block reading an ambient script-scoped name, so its value depended on when the block ran.
A published artifact whose collection field was serialized as a scalar.
